name: manual_cf3a7a
claim: Python sqlite3's 'with connection:' context manager only commits or rolls back on exit -- it never closes the underlying connection. Every prior call site in tier5_budget.py that did 'with self._connect() as db:' leaked one connection per call, relying on GC finalization instead of an explicit close. Fix: a small contextmanager combining both -- 'db = self._connect(); try: with db: yield db; finally: db.close()' -- gives correct commit/rollback AND guaranteed close from one call site, replacing N near-duplicate connect/BEGIN/commit blocks.
conditions: sqlite3 connection leak with-statement context manager close transaction commit rollback python stdlib gotcha

decisions.notes: 2026-08-21, PT PR #359 CodeRabbit review #4983381866, fixed in commit 1d56a095. Caught during a batch review of a SQLite-backed ledger module -- five methods each opened a fresh connection with no matching close(). Worth a standing instinct: any 'with self._connect() as db:' pattern in this codebase is a leak unless paired with an explicit close, since sqlite3.Connection's context-manager protocol only covers the transaction, not the resource.
